contracts.signal: Siemens provides the electrical distribution, protection, automation and controls to the NVIDIA DSX AI-factory reference architecture - 'from the grid connection to the AI rack' - and the digital twin customers use to design, build and operate the facility; Siemens, NVIDIA and ecosystem partners introduced the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin Reference Design for the U.S. and European markets, translating DSX requirements into deployable power and controls infrastructure.

quarterly_data.quarter: Siemens press release: Siemens and NVIDIA are advancing Industrial AI (10-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI factory infrastructure and industrial AI with NVIDIA (release): Siemens and Delta co-designed prefabricated, factory-tested electrical power modules that the release says can reduce data-center time to market by up to 50 percent; Siemens' physics-based digital twin, built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, models grid interaction, cooling shortfalls and cooling-equipment noise before construction. In engineering, Simcenter on NVIDIA accelerated computing runs supported simulations up to ten times faster and Simcenter PhysicsAI predicts design performance up to 1,000 times faster than traditional simulation; in manufacturing, an initial customer deployment of AI-powered factory scheduling increased throughput by 20 percent.
quarterly_data.figure: prefabricated power modules: data-center time to market reduced by up to 50 percent

quarterly_data.signal: EDA with NVIDIA (release): Siemens and NVIDIA developed AI agents that automate complex chip-design tasks and verify their results using Siemens' EDA tools and NVIDIA AI infrastructure; Siemens' AI-driven electrothermal workflow, accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, predicts heat build-up in stacked chips before manufacturing, sets up multiple tools in under five minutes instead of several days and enables 50 times more design exploration than manual methods (company figures).
